evidence: src/business/services/OrderService.ts placeOrder: coordinates the use case, enforces the NOT_FOUND rules through BusinessError, calls product.reserve(item.quantity) and applies pricing.discountFor(...). These are domain/service responsibilities.
src/business/services/OrderService.ts cancelOrder: calls order.cancel() and puts stock back through products.updateStock. Storage is left to the gateway; no persistence mechanism lives in this file.
src/business/services/OrderService.ts mapping from records to domain objects (toProduct, toOrder, toOrderRecord, toCustomer) is handed to RecordMapping rather than done here.
There is no SQL, HTTP, serialization or framework code anywhere in the file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: OrderService is a Fowler-style Service Layer in the business (domain) layer. Everything it does is use-case coordination and business rules. placeOrder checks that the customer and products exist, reserves stock through the domain method product.reserve, builds OrderLine and Order objects and applies the PricingPolicy discount. cancelOrder calls the domain method order.cancel() and puts the stock back. getOrder fetches an order and maps it into a domain object. Reading and writing data is handed to the injected gateways, and turning records into domain objects is handed to RecordMapping. The file contains no SQL, connection or transaction handling, HTTP, request/response handling or framework code. The id generator nextId() and the helper sumOf() are simple domain-side logic. The file imports the gateways from src/persistence, but that is an import-direction concern and outside the scope of this rule. One small point: cancelOrder works out the restored stock straight from the raw record (record.stock + line.quantity) rather than through a domain object. That is still business logic, though, and does not belong to another layer kind.
